items.title: Cosimo Matassa Interview, 1993-07-17
items.q: I remember once, I sent him a bill. In fact, it was a Fats Domino session.

ctx.x: You know? He was sometimes downright mean-spirited with people. Even me. I remember once, I sent him a bill. In fact, it was a Fats Domino session. In those days, the early days, I was only charging $15 an hour for the studio. Fifteen? The studio and me, both, okay? Fifteen bucks an hour. And I sent the bill, and he sent me back a letter, without using those words, saying I overcharged him. And he said things like, well, there are studios out here that make yours sound like crap and all that. And I only paid $35…
Wow. Yeah. Well, anyone else come to mind from the early days?

items.title: Cosimo Matassa Interview, 1994-01-15
items.q: But, but Al was in at the very beginning on the Fats Domino stuff.

ctx.x: Well, in, in that he's the one that got Fats recorded with, uh, uh, uh, Imperial. Mm-hmm. You know, uh, Al had, was working for Apollo and, uh, another couple of labels down here, down here. Selling the records and, and looking for talent and doing things with them. And how, I, I don't know. I, I never asked him how he and Lou got together and all that. But, but Al was in at the very beginning on the Fats Domino stuff. And then he got shut out. Somewhere along the way.
He, he, he brought Fats to Lou? He, he.

items.title: Cosimo Matassa Interview, 1993-11-01
items.q: what was the thing Fast Downbone did?

ctx.x: And he did, and also he did, what was the thing Fast Downbone did? Marty Grudin. Marty Grudin.
